tour.description: VoxLane is a multi-tenant AI voice receptionist SaaS, first piloted with Porto Douro Restaurants. CLAUDE.md sits at the project root and is the canonical onboarding brief: it explains the two-service split (Go voice-gateway + NestJS backend), the lock file, the do-not-touch runtime boundaries, and where to find deeper specs. Read it first to learn what the platform promises tenants and which subsystems are stable versus experimental.

tour.title: Voice Gateway Entry Point
tour.description: The Go binary in voice-gateway/cmd/gateway/main.go is the runtime's front door: it boots the HTTP/WebSocket server, instantiates provider adapters from config, and dispatches audio relay handlers per call. Config is loaded once from environment variables via voice-gateway/internal/config/config.go, which validates provider/renderer/codec combinations before the gateway accepts a single connection. Together these two files answer 'how does a VoxLane call start?'

tour.title: Audio Codec Pipeline
tour.description: Telephony audio arrives as G.711 A-law or mu-law at 8 kHz, but the LLM and TTS services want 16 kHz PCM. The internal/audio package performs that translation: pipeline.go wires the steps, g722.go handles the G.722 wideband codec, mulaw.go and alaw.go implement the G.711 decoders, and resampler.go does the sample-rate conversion. Understanding this layer is essential because every other gateway subsystem consumes AudioFrame values produced here.

tour.title: Provider Adapters
tour.description: Twilio, Telnyx, and SignalWire each expose calls through their own wire protocols, so the gateway hides them behind a single Adapter interface defined in internal/provider/provider.go. The concrete adapters (twilio/adapter.go, telnyx/adapter.go, signalwire/adapter.go) translate provider events into the gateway's AudioFrame/Event/CallControlResponse vocabulary. Selecting a provider is just a config flag; the rest of the gateway never branches on vendor.

tour.title: Session Orchestrator
tour.description: internal/session/session.go is the largest and most-imported file in the gateway (top of both fan-in and fan-out rankings). It owns the per-call state machine loop: it ingests audio frames from a provider adapter, runs VAD, calls the LLM runtime, fetches TTS, paces outbound mulaw, and persists checkpoints to the Redis session store. Every other session sub-file (booking, state-machine, capture helpers) is a collaborator that the orchestrator composes into a single call lifecycle.

tour.title: State Machine and Booking Slots
tour.description: The state machine in internal/session/sm/state_machine.go tracks where a caller is in the conversation (greeting, slot-filling, confirmation, handoff), and internal/session/booking_slots.go parses spoken date/time/party-size answers into the structured booking object the backend later persists. These two files encode the receptionist's domain logic â€” without them the orchestrator would just be a generic voice pipe.

tour.title: TTS Renderer (Cartesia)
tour.description: internal/renderer/renderer.go defines a renderer-agnostic interface, and internal/renderer/cartesia/renderer.go is the current production implementation that streams Cartesia's low-latency TTS into the gateway. The orchestrator calls Renderer.Synthesize to turn LLM text into audio, and the codec pipeline from Step 3 then converts that audio into the format the active provider expects. This is the most recent architectural pin â€” earlier voice-stack decisions live alongside it in docs/VOICE-STACK-DECISION-MATRIX.md.

tour.title: NestJS Backend API
tour.description: The TypeScript backend lives in backend/src. main.ts boots the Nest application, app.module.ts wires feature modules together, and modules/voice/voice.controller.ts receives Twilio webhooks that the voice-gateway forwards when a call needs booking persistence or tool execution. A shared HMAC guard (common/guards/hmac.guard.ts) verifies the signature on every inbound webhook so tenants cannot impersonate each other. This is the persistence and tooling half of the platform.

tour.title: Shared TypeScript Types
tour.description: shared/src is a small package of TypeScript types (index.ts re-exports them) covering booking, session, tenant, and tools shapes. Both the NestJS backend and any future TypeScript consumer â€” including admin UIs or SDK clients â€” depend on this package so booking objects look identical across the wire. Treat this directory as the public contract between the voice-gateway's outbound payloads and the backend's inbound handlers.

tour.title: Deployment and Runtime
tour.description: Production runs as two containers orchestrated by docker-compose.yml: the voice-gateway image built from service:voice-gateway/Dockerfile (multi-stage, builder + alpine) and the NestJS backend. Caddy (config:deploy/Caddyfile.example) terminates TLS and routes public webhooks to the right container, while the systemd unit (config:deploy/systemd/voice-gateway.service.example) shows the equivalent on-metal layout. This is the file set you will touch when a new tenant is onboarded to a fresh VPS.

tour.title: Where to Look Next
tour.description: Two documents capture the live state of the platform. docs/context/VOXLANE_MASTER_CONTEXT.md is the deep architectural brief â€” multi-tenancy, voice-stack strategy, runtime lock, and the active MVP scope. docs/VPS_DEPLOYMENT_RUNBOOK.md is the operational counterpart: it walks through deploying a fresh VPS with Caddy, systemd, and the voice-gateway. Start with MASTER_CONTEXT, then keep the runbook open whenever you are about to ship.

tour.title: Multi-Vendor Voice Spike (2026-06-10)
tour.description: The user approved building a multi-vendor voice pipeline scaffold to A/B test Deepgram (STT), xAI Grok (LLM), ElevenLabs (TTS), Cerebras (LLM), LiveKit (transport), and Redis (memory) against the xAI single-vendor baseline. Three bundles are pre-built. Vendor SDKs are NOT installed yet. Read DECISION_REPORT_MULTI_VENDOR.md first, then the spike scaffold.
